patients.summary: Retired accountant with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, LAD-stented coronary disease, HFrEF, CKD 3b and a 2017 stroke who joins in 2019. Lumbar stenosis, then systemic AL amyloidosis treated with Dara-CyBorD, oropharyngeal dysphagia, a hydrochlorothiazide reaction, polymyositis on prednisone and azathioprine, ischemic hepatitis in 2023 and heart failure admissions in 2024 and 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

67-year-old man, retired accountant, moving his care here from another primary care office. Wanted a doctor he can reach by phone between visits. Records release signed today.

HPI / history as he tells it:
- Blood pressure for many years, on lisinopril and amlodipine. Home cuff usually low 130s.
- Type 2 diabetes for about a decade, metformin only. No lows. Checks sugar a few times a week, fasting 130s-150s.
- Coronary disease. Had a heart cath in 2015 and a drug-eluting stent placed in the LAD the same admission. No chest pain since. Aspirin daily.
- Heart failure with a weak pump; was told at his last echo (2018) the squeeze was "about 40 percent." On furosemide 40 every morning. Sleeps on one pillow, no swelling most days.
- Kidneys: told he is stage 3b, followed with blood work by his old office.
- Stroke 2017. Left him with mild weakness of the left arm and hand. Slow with buttons and jar lids, otherwise fully independent. Drives.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, furosemide 40 mg qAM, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: cardiac cath with LAD DES, 2015.
FH: Father - MI at 62, also hypertension. Mother - type 2 diabetes, stroke at 70. Nobody in the family with amyloidosis or autoimmune disease that he knows of.
SH: Retired accountant. Never smoked. Used to have an occasional drink; none for years. No drugs. Walks most days.

ROS: No chest pain, palpitations, syncope. No orthopnea or PND. No change in bowel habits. No urinary symptoms beyond nocturia x1. Remainder negative.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. Pleasant, NAD.
HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, JVP not elevated, no carotid bruits.
Heart regular, normal S1/S2, no murmur or gallop.
Lungs clear bilaterally.
Abdomen soft, nontender.
Ext: no edema. DP/PT pulses 2+ bilaterally.
Neuro: alert, fluent speech. Mild weakness of left grip and finger extension; strength otherwise full including both legs. Gait steady without device.
Feet: skin intact, no calluses or ulcers, monofilament intact both feet.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension - at goal today. Continue lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5.
2. T2DM with CKD - A1c and urine albumin/creatinine today. Continue metformin 1000 BID.
3. CAD s/p LAD stent (2015) - asymptomatic. Continue aspirin 81.
4. HFrEF - euvolemic on exam. Continue furosemide 40. Will review his old echo when records arrive.
5. CKD 3b - CMP today to set his baseline here.
6. Prior ischemic stroke (2017), mild residual weakness of the left arm and hand - stable.
7. Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2016 per patient, normal. Tdap 2016. HD flu shot when it arrives next month. Hep C and HIV screening today. Shingrix series this winter. PSA discussed; he does not want screening.

Return 3 months, sooner as needed. Portal set up today.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mr. Clark,

Your blood work from Tuesday is back. Kidney function is in the same range your previous office has been seeing, so nothing new there. Your A1c is a little over 7, which is a good level for you. Blood counts are normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative.

The urine test shows a modest amount of protein leaking through the kidneys. That is common with diabetes and blood pressure, and the lisinopril you already take is the right medicine for it. We will repeat it once a year.

See you in December.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records Received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Outside records reviewed (prior primary care office, ~180 pages, scanned to Media).

Pertinent items:
- Cardiac catheterization, 2015, outside hospital: diagnostic study followed by drug-eluting stent to the LAD the same sitting. Aspirin continued.
- Hospital discharge summary, 2017: acute ischemic stroke; discharged home with mild residual weakness of the left arm and hand.
- Transthoracic echo, 2018: LVEF 40%.
- Problem list matches what he reported: HTN, T2DM, CAD, HFrEF, CKD stage 3b, prior stroke.
- Medication list matches current five medications.
- Colonoscopy 2016: no polyps, repeat in 10 years.
- Tdap 2016. No Shingrix on file. Pneumococcal records not found.
- Creatinine over the last two years in the 1.8-1.9 range.

Problem list here updated. Nothing to act on.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu vaccine. No fever today, no prior reactions. High-dose quadrivalent influenza 0.7 mL IM left deltoid, lot/expiration in the immunization record. VIS reviewed. Waited 15 minutes, no issues.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home in Southampton, identity confirmed, consents to telehealth.

Has been staying home except for groceries early in the morning. Feels fine. Walks the road in front of his house. Home BP log (read to me): 124-138 / 72-84. Weights steady 184-186 lb at home. Fasting sugars 128-150. No chest pain, no orthopnea, no swelling. Mail-order meds arriving fine.

Observed: comfortable, speaking full sentences, no visible distress.

A/P:
- HTN, HFrEF, T2DM, CKD 3b: stable by history and home data. No changes.
- Labs at the draw station this week: BMP, A1c, urine albumin/creatinine.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT (initial)

Health risk assessment reviewed. Lives in Southampton, independent in ADLs and IADLs, still drives, manages his own finances and medications (pill organizer). No falls in the past year. Hearing adequate in conversation. Vision corrected, eye exam yearly. PHQ-2 0.
Diet: trying to limit sweets and salt. Activity: walks most days.

Current problems: HTN, T2DM with CKD, CAD s/p LAD stent, HFrEF, CKD 3b, prior stroke with mild left arm/hand weakness.
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40, ASA 81. NKDA.

Exam: weight stable. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. No edema. Get-up-and-go normal.

Prevention:
- Colon: colonoscopy 2016 normal, next 2026.
- Shingrix complete (1/2020, 3/2020).
- Tdap 2016.
- Flu shot this fall.
- Pneumococcal: no record; will give when supply allows.
- Hep C / HIV screened 2019.
- PSA: declines, reviewed again.

Labs today: lipids, CMP, CBC.
Personalized prevention plan given in writing.

documents.title: Office Visit - Back Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: back pain going into both legs.

HPI: Since about March, aching in the low back that travels into the backs of both thighs. Comes on after he has been walking or standing for a while, e.g. 15-20 minutes in line or walking the road. Sitting down settles it within minutes. Notices he can do the whole grocery store if he leans on the cart. No numbness, no tingling below the knees, no bowel or bladder change, no saddle numbness. No fever, no weight loss. No injury. Has avoided ibuprofen because of his kidneys; tried a heating pad.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40, ASA 81. NKDA.

Exam: walks without antalgia. Lumbar spine without point tenderness. Lumbar range of motion comfortable. Straight leg raise negative both sides. Hip range of motion full and painless. Leg strength 5/5 bilaterally, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, sensation intact. DP/PT pulses palpable bilaterally.

A/P: Back and posterior thigh pain with standing and walking, relieved by sitting and forward flexion, normal pulses - sounds neurogenic rather than vascular claudication; suspect lumbar spinal stenosis.
- MRI lumbar spine without contrast.
- Neurology referral.
- No NSAIDs given CKD. Activity as tolerated.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose quadrivalent flu vaccine 0.7 mL IM right deltoid. Masked visit, screening questions negative. Tolerated well. Reminded of MRI next week.

reports.text:
MRI LUMBAR SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Indication: Low back pain radiating to both posterior thighs with walking and standing.
Technique: Sagittal T1, T2 and STIR; axial T2 images through the lumbar spine.
Findings: Lumbar alignment is maintained. Vertebral body heights are preserved and marrow signal is normal. The conus terminates normally. The lumbar spinal canal is narrowed, with degenerative change of the facet joints and thickening of the ligamentum flavum contributing. Paraspinal soft tissues are unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lumbar spinal canal narrowing with facet degenerative change and ligamentum flavum hypertrophy.

documents.title: MRI Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: MRI lumbar spine shows a narrowed spinal canal from facet arthritis and a thickened ligamentum flavum, consistent with his symptoms. Neurology appointment 10/29 - copy of report sent. Called patient and explained.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 10/29/2020
Referred by: primary care

Reason for referral: low back pain into both legs with walking.

History: Mr. Clark is a 68-year-old man who for roughly six months has had low back pain spreading into the posterior thighs on both sides. Prolonged standing or walking brings it on; sitting, or bending forward over a shopping cart, relieves it. No sensory symptoms in the feet, no sphincter change.

Past history: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, coronary artery disease with LAD stent, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, CKD stage 3b, ischemic stroke 2017 with mild residual left arm and hand weakness.
Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: father MI at 62 and hypertension; mother type 2 diabetes and stroke at 70; no amyloidosis or autoimmune disease.
Social: retired accountant, never smoker, no alcohol now.

Examination: Lower extremity strength is full throughout. Peripheral pulses present and symmetric. Straight leg raise negative on both sides. Reflexes symmetric. Sensation preserved to light touch and vibration in both feet. Mild left hand weakness consistent with his old stroke. Gait narrow-based and steady.

Imaging: MRI lumbar spine (10/13/2020) reviewed - narrowed canal with facet degenerative change and ligamentum flavum hypertrophy.

Impression: Lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication. No deficit to suggest a need for surgical referral at this point.

Recommendations:
1. Physical therapy for a flexion-based program.
2. Acetaminophen 500-1000 mg up to three times a day as needed. Avoid NSAIDs given his kidney function.
3. Return as needed; spine surgery opinion if symptoms progress or a deficit develops.

Thank you for this referral.
Neurology

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Neurology letter received and reviewed: lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication, conservative care. Called patient. PT referral sent to the outpatient PT clinic he prefers. Acetaminophen as neurology suggested; no NSAIDs. He is relieved it is "not my heart." Problem list updated.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
PHYSICAL THERAPY INITIAL EVALUATION
Date of service: 11/12/2020
Diagnosis: lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication (referral from primary care, neurology recommendation).

Subjective: Back and posterior thigh pain after 15-20 minutes on his feet, eased by sitting or leaning forward. Goal: walk the length of the grocery store and his road without stopping.
Relevant history: CAD with stent, heart failure, CKD, prior stroke with mild left hand weakness. Allergies: none known.

Objective: Lumbar extension provokes back pain; flexion relieves. Lower extremity strength grossly 5/5. Neuro screen intact. Walked 6 minutes on treadmill before symptoms; tolerated longer with slight incline.

Assessment: Presentation consistent with lumbar stenosis. Good rehab potential.

Plan: 2x/week for 6 weeks - flexion-biased exercises, hip flexor stretching, core strengthening, stationary bike for conditioning, home program. Monitor for exertional symptoms given cardiac history.
